Heard.
(2) In both these revisions order dated 20.10.2010
passed by Civil Judge (Senior Division) Nainital, in
Suit No. 133 of 2008 is challenged, whereby said
court has dismissed the application No. 22C moved
by the defendant No.1 and 37C moved by the
defendant No.15.
(3) Brief facts of the case are that the respondent
No.1 Thakur Dan Singh Bist Trust and respondent
No.2 I.S. Rathor (trustee) filed Suit No. 133 of 2008
for mandatory injunction the defendants directing to
handover the vacant possession of the apartments
known as Grassmere Lake Apartments in Nainital to
the plaintiffs. It is also prayed that he defendants be
directed to pay damages for the unauthorized
occupation. The case of the present revisionists is
that they have no concern with the property in suit,
and they are unnecessarily impleaded by the
plaintiffs.

6
(4) In the application 22C it is alleged by the
defendant No.1 that apartments No. F1 is actually
owned by one Smt. Daya W/o Shri Bhagwan Singh
C-11 215, Sector 3, Rohini, New Delhi 85 and the
present defendant No.1 has no concern with said flat.
Similarly, the defendant No.15 in his application 37C
has pleaded before the trial court that said defendant
is not concern with flat No. UG4, UG5 and UG6
which are being held by Maiher Cement Century
Textile Industries, Post Office Sarla Nagar, Maihar,
District Satna (Madhya Pradesh).
(5) Having heard learned counsel for the
revisionists, and after going through the impugned
order, I agree with the trial court to the extent that the
plaintiffs cannot be compelled to delete defendant
No.1 and defendant No.15 from the array of parties
as the allegation made by the plaintiffs against the
defendants are denied by the then and the
truthfulness of the same is to be decided by trial
court. But as far as the impleadment of the parties
relating to whom the defendants have made specific
pleas that they are the persons to whom the alleged
flats were transferred by registered sale deed, this
court thinks it just and proper to observe that the
trial court may frame issues alongwith other issues

7
regarding to the fact whether such parties are proper
or necessary for the just decision of the case, and if it
comes to the conclusion, that such parties as pointed
out by defendant No.1 and defendant No.15 are
proper or necessary parties to be impleaded in the
suit, the trial court may pass necessary orders as it
thinks fit during proceedings of the suit.
(6) With the above observations these two
revisions stand disposed of. (Misc. Application No.
4286 of 2013 and Misc. Application No. 4287 of
2013 also stand disposed of).
(Prafulla C. Pant, J.)
Dt.24.06.2013
